sections.h2: Where is Florence County and who lives there?
sections.html:
Florence County is in the Pee Dee region of northeastern South Carolina, and the city of Florence is both its seat and its largest community. The county covers 804.28 square miles, of which 800.51 are land, and the 2020 census counted 137,059 people in 54,627 households.

Three municipalities are named: Florence, Johnsonville and Lake City. The Pee Dee and Lynches rivers are the main waterways, and the county holds Lynches River County Park, part of Moore Farms Botanical Garden, part of Woods Bay State Park and the Pee Dee Station Site Wildlife Management Area. Eight counties touch its borders: Marlboro, Dillon, Marion, Williamsburg, Clarendon, Sumter, Lee and Darlington.

The county was founded in 1888 from sections of Darlington and Marion counties, plus townships from Williamsburg and Clarendon. It took its name from its seat, which William Harllee named for his daughter. The last section of Williamsburg County was added in 1921.

That patchwork history shows up in parcel records. A house inside the city of Florence also carries city tax, with the rate set by City Council by June 30 each year, so two similar homes in different parts of the county can see different bills. Read the millage lines on the bill, not only the county total.

sections.h2: What jobs support Florence County housing?
sections.html:
Health care leads, followed by retail. Health care and social assistance make up 22.9 percent of employment and retail trade 13.3 percent. The county's 2022 gross domestic product was $8.5 billion, and unemployment ranged from 2.3 to 3.8 percent across 2022 to 2024.

The largest employers named for the county are:

  • Duke Energy
  • Francis Marion University
  • GE HealthCare
  • Honda
  • McLeod Health
  • Otis Worldwide
  • QVC
  • Ruiz Foods
  • Walmart

sections.h2: When are Florence County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate and most personal property taxes are due by January 15. If a deadline falls on a weekend or holiday it generally moves to the next business day. Bills usually go out around October.

The Treasurer does not calculate taxes or apply penalties. The Auditor does that, and the Treasurer has to collect the full amount on the notice. The county says partial payments are not accepted, postmarks are honored, and an unavailable online service does not delay a penalty. Receipts are dated the day the payment is processed.

State law gives one relief: if title passed during the tax year, the notice went to the prior owner and the new owner got no timely notice, the treasurer shall waive the penalties. Do not rely on it. Confirm the bill's mailing address with the Assessor after any sale.

sections.h2: How do you pay and who do you call in Florence County?
sections.html:
You can pay in person, by mail or online. Mail goes to Florence County Treasurer, P.O. Box 100501, Florence, SC 29502-0501, and the county complex is at 180 N Irby Street, Florence, SC 29501. County offices there are open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

  • Treasurer: 843-665-3041. Collects the bill. Treasurer Laurie Walsh Carpenter was elected in 2016 and also serves as tax collector.
  • Tax Assessor: 843-665-3056. Legal residence, address changes, mobile home registrations, deeds and plats.
  • Auditor: 843-665-3088. Homestead exemption, bill calculation and penalties.
  • Delinquent Tax Collection: 843-665-3095. Payoff amounts and tax sale redemption.

Cards are accepted in person with ID and a signature, with a processor fee of 1.7 percent plus $1. Online payments go through PayStar, which adds its own fee, and the official receipt arrives by mail in 5 to 10 business days. Delinquent taxes cannot be paid online. Use cash, a cashier's check or a money order, or a card in person. See the county's Treasurer page.

sections.h2: How does reassessment work in Florence County?
sections.html:
South Carolina requires each county to reassess all real property every five years at current market value. In a reassessment year the taxable value of a parcel cannot rise more than 15 percent over five years unless an assessable transfer of interest happens, which is the usual result of a sale.

The county must also lower its millage to a rollback rate when total values climb, though a single bill can still go up or down. Taxpayers are notified of changes of $1,000 or more. The Assessor's page describes the reassessment for tax year 2024 and says appeals had to be in writing by January 15. The appeal form on the site carries a 2027 label, so ask the office which cycle applies to you before you plan around any deadline.

For an appeal outside a notice window, state law lets you object in writing within 90 days after the assessor mails a notice. The county also offers qPublic for parcel records and a tax estimator on its site, which help a buyer or seller see what a new owner might owe.

sections.h2: What does a legal residence application need in Florence County?
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office asks the applicant and spouse for a South Carolina driver's license or state ID, vehicle registration and a voter registration card where they apply, and a Social Security card. These requirements took effect June 20, 2016.

The page gives no filing deadline for legal residence. The Auditor's Office separately handles the Homestead Exemption Program and has an application form. Ask the Assessor how a new owner applies after a sale, since the page does not say.

sections.h2: What happens at a Florence County tax sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid real property goes to a public auction run by the Delinquent Tax Office. The 2026 sale was scheduled to start Monday, October 5, 2026, at 10:00 a.m., with pre-registration due October 2 and a $10 bidder fee.

The owner or a mortgage holder has one year and a day to redeem. The county listed the 2026 redemption deadline as October 6, 2027, with interest added quarterly at 3, 6, 9 and 12 percent of the bid. If nobody redeems, a tax deed is issued, and the county warns that it is not a warranty deed and liens can remain.

Costs rise during the year. The county's list of 2025 amounts includes $20 for delinquent notices in March, $30 for certified mail of a levy in April, $25 for advertising in August and $60 for a land mortgage search in October. Call 843-665-3095 to confirm the amount before paying, because dates and costs can change.

sections.h2: What should a Florence County seller know about the land and weather?
sections.html:
The county sits on the coastal plain, and the neighboring counties show how a big storm can matter here. During Hurricane Florence in 2018 the Pee Dee River crested at 46.51 feet at Cheraw, and flooding hit Marion and Dillon counties next door. Wikipedia's account does not describe Florence County flooding, so check each parcel's flood status instead of assuming.

The city of Florence has a humid subtropical climate with very hot, humid summers, and I-20 and I-95 meet there. Florence Regional Airport is about two miles east of downtown, which helps owners who live elsewhere and manage a sale from a distance.

faqs.q: What is the Florence County property tax penalty schedule?
faqs.a: Taxes unpaid after January 15 pick up 3 percent on January 16, another 7 percent on February 2 and another 5 percent on March 17, for 15 percent plus collection costs.

faqs.q: Can I make a partial property tax payment in Florence County?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer says it must collect the full amount shown on the tax notice, including penalties, and partial payments are not accepted.

faqs.q: Where is the Florence County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: The county complex is at 180 N Irby Street in Florence, and the Treasurer's phone is 843-665-3041. Mail payments to P.O. Box 100501, Florence, SC 29502-0501.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem a Florence County tax sale property?
faqs.a: The owner or mortgage holder has one year and a day after the sale. Interest is added in quarterly steps.

faqs.q: Who handles appeals in Florence County?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor handles appeals, which must be written. State law sets a 90 day window after the assessor mails a notice. Call 843-665-3056 for the current form.
